k.q: Trace a function calculating uncompressed image pixel data using two parameters.
k.code:
function imageBits(pixels,depth)
    return pixels * depth
endfunction
print(imageBits(50,8))
p: Predict the returned number of bits.
Change depth from 8 to 16 in the call.
Explain what colour depth means and why a function returns the result.
k.a: imageBits(50,8) returns 400 bits. Passing 16 bits per pixel returns 800 bits. Colour depth is the number of bits used to encode each image pixel; returning a result allows the caller to reuse it (e.g. convert bits to bytes). This excludes metadata and compression.

e: Explain one difference between a function and a procedure. [2 marks]
A function returns a value; a procedure performs statements without necessarily returning a value.
State the role of parameters. [2 marks]
They pass input values into a subprogram.
Give one benefit of modular programming. [2 marks]
Reduces duplication, simplifies testing or maintenance.

stretch.task: Call imageBits with two different colour depths, then convert each result into bytes.
stretch.hint: Call imageBits(50,8) and imageBits(50,16); divide each returned bit count by 8.
stretch.answer: 50 pixels at 8 bits/pixel → 400 bits = 50 bytes. At 16 bits/pixel → 800 bits = 100 bytes, excluding metadata.
